title: Life Swap
text: “So fast… wow, Kuro-chan, incredible.”
“Mm…”
“There’s still not enough vitality recovered. Allow me to lend my strength as well. Life Swap.”

The Siltvelt envoy cast a spell. Apparently it was magic that shared one’s own life force with another—a natural aptitude possessed by many demi-humans and beastmen. I’d brought the Siltvelt envoy along more or less on a whim, but it turned out to be the right call, I say.
“Pfah… ugh… hoo… *cough*…”
Big Sister’s friend’s breathing steadied a little, though the coughing hadn’t quite stopped yet.
“Now we just need to use direct healing magic to speed things along, indeed. Father’s magic would be better suited for this sort of thing, but this should barely manage to pull it off.”
Even with my healing magic and medicine, the symptoms were improving slowly—which just goes to show how close to death this child truly was. Truly right on the razor’s edge of dying, I’d wager.
“T-thank you very much.”
The utterly worn-out Big Sister offered her thanks to us.
“Not me—thank Motoyasu-kun.”
“No, no, Father will do just fine, I say.”

Well then, it had been quite a dangerous situation, but we’d managed some manner of first aid. Now the priority was eliminating the greatest obstacle. Right now these girls were bound by slave crests. Taking them out of here carelessly would be dangerous, so that had to be dealt with first. I headed for the exit of the cell.
“Kuro-chan, I’ll leave guarding Father and the others to you, indeed.”
“Uuu… Kuro wanted to play assassin too, but okay.”
“Assassin, she says…”

“I would like to capture him and make him suffer the same fate… but given the state of these children, it’s probably better than risking them being taken hostage. Spear Hero-sama, will you require assistance?”
“Unnecessary. I shall swiftly erase every trace of that man’s existence from this world. Not even a corpse shall remain, I say.”

Clack, clack—I strode out of the cell, and using Cloaking Lance and wall-phasing, went searching for the noble who’d been conducting the torture. It seemed he was in his private chambers within the mansion. He’d apparently just returned from an outing and was in the middle of preparing to head off for another round of torture.
“Now then, is that brat dead? If it’s still alive, I suppose I’ll finish it off… heh heh heh.”
So it seemed he was contemplating one final bout of torture. Muttering to himself—what a repulsive man. Well then, without even realizing he’d died… die, I say!
“Wh-what?! GYAAAH—!?”

Burst Lance risked being noticed no matter how much I muffled the sound, and firing off Brionac indoors was out of the question, so I scorched the designated spot with Liberation Firefloor X instead. I’d really wanted to torture him properly, but instead I obliterated him without a trace, not even leaving a corpse. Not quite like Kuro-chan’s methods, but for the good of the world, for the good of mankind, for the good of society, I made him vanish—quite literally.
“Now then, shall we?”
With that settled, I entered the room and skewered the dead noble’s soul with Soul Eater Spear.
“Well then, off we go, I say.”

Dragging along the noble’s soul, who surely had no idea what was happening, I phased straight down through the wall into the basement. Landing with a soft thump in the cellar, I rejoined Father and the others and made a point of showing the noble’s soul the girls we’d rescued.
“Wha— this is—?!”
“I really would have liked to torture you properly, but time is short, so I’ll let you off with just this little viewing, I say. Farewell, then.”
“Damn you! GYAAAH—”
And with that, I yanked him right out and tore him into scattered little pieces.
“I’m back.”
“Welcome back, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Was the noble here made to answer for his crimes?”
The Siltvelt envoy asked, so I nodded firmly. I’d made sure to show him the rescued girls properly before finishing him off, after all.
“Naturally, I say.”
Now then, I turned to check on the girls—Father was holding Big Sister’s hand, but where was Big Sister’s friend? Just then, I noticed Kuro-chan in her Filolial form had her feathers all puffed up.
“This kid’s riding on Kuro’s back.”
“Oh, splendid, indeed.”
Wrapped up in natural down to keep her body warm, I see.
“Well then, time to withdraw. Shall we make a flashy exit or a quiet one?”
Perhaps a grand finish, to mark that this time was different from before?
“Proving our valor loud and clear is certainly one option, I say.”
“Ehh… I’d rather we keep this quiet, if possible. You said the ringleader’s already been made to answer for it, right?”
“Naturally. I obliterated him completely, indeed!”
I gave a firm thumbs-up.
“Obliterated…”
Father muttered, his expression suggesting he didn’t quite grasp the details but was sure something impressive had happened.
“Then a quiet escape it is. Big Sister’s friend’s consciousness is likely too clouded for portal travel to work smoothly—she’ll need to be registered in the party first, indeed.”
“I see. Then… let’s go.”
And so we made our quiet escape. We slipped out of town under cover of stealth and released it once we were clear.
“First, let’s prioritize treatment. Well done enduring all this, so young.”

The Siltvelt envoy spoke gently to the girls. After that, we spent about half a day outside the town treating Big Sister’s friend. With me and the Siltvelt envoy periodically casting healing magic and having her take medicine, Big Sister’s friend eventually regained consciousness.
“Where… am I…”
“Rifana-chan! Thank goodness. Help came.”
Big Sister held her friend’s hand and explained everything.
“Thank goodness. Looks like things worked out somehow… It’s frustrating just watching, though.”

Father lamented, though there was nothing to be done about that. Still, thanks to the effects of the Shield’s released power boosting the potency of the medicine she’d been taking, he hadn’t been merely watching after all.
“For now, let’s transport her somewhere capable of proper treatment. I’d like to invite her to join the party, if she’ll accept, indeed.”
I extended the invitation to Big Sister’s now-conscious friend and had her join.
“Using a treatment facility in Melromarc would be difficult, indeed.”
Given Trash’s tyrannical authority still holding sway in Melromarc, specialized treatment there would be a tough ask.
“She’s more or less past the worst of it, so we could secure a powerful healing potion within a few days. What would you like to do, indeed?”
“Saving her life comes first. If we could get her treatment in Siltvelt…”
“I agree. Though… if we bring this child to Siltvelt for treatment and explain the circumstances…”
The Siltvelt envoy trailed off, choosing words carefully.
“You mean it could get seized on as propaganda for Siltvelt’s invasion, right? Something like ‘the Heroes rescued these frail children—do not forgive Melromarc!’”
“Yes. Given how monstrous this has been… it would likely lead to war.”
It wasn’t as though we couldn’t simply handle it swiftly, but this was indeed an unprecedented course of action.
“I’d rather avoid that if possible. Part of me wants to see them get what’s coming, but I don’t want to drag uninvolved people into a conflict.”
Ah, truly like Father to say such a thing.
“Could you keep it under wraps using Hero authority?”
“Perhaps, but I can’t guarantee it.”
“Then Zeltoble would be best—it’ll cost a bit of money, but we can have her treated there, indeed.”
Covering the friend’s treatment costs would be a trivial matter, easily earned within a few days.
“We can go to Zeltoble too? Then that settles it. They won’t pry too deeply into the circumstances there.”
“Then let’s be off! Portal Spear, indeed!”
And so, we made our temporary leap to Zeltoble.
